title: The clap back that wasn't

verse.sanskrit:
पापानां वा शुभानां वा वधार्हाणां प्लवङ्गम ।
कार्यं करुणमार्येण न कश्चिन्नापराध्यति ॥
verse.iast:
pāpānāṃ vā śubhānāṃ vā vadhārhāṇāṃ plavaṅgama |
kāryaṃ karuṇam āryeṇa na kaścin nāparādhyati ||
verse.translation: Whether they are wicked or good, or even deserve to die, O monkey, a noble person should act with compassion; there is no one who never does wrong.

beats.title: you finally get to CLAP BACK
beats.vo: The war is over. The people who scared you every single day are right in front of you. And it's your call.

beats.title: PLOT TWIST
beats.vo: Hanuman brings Sita the news: Ravana is gone. Then he asks: just say the word, and I'll punish every guard who threatened you.
Sita says no. They were just following Ravana's orders. With him gone, they won't scare anyone again.
Wicked or good, even those who deserve punishment, a noble person acts with compassion. No one never makes mistakes.
Mercy isn't weak. It's what the strongest person in the room chooses.
So when the bully, the toxic coworker, or the ex finally slips up, you don't have to pile on. Win, then let it go.

beats.title: Day 16 of learning from Rama
beats.vo: Day sixteen of learning from Rama, and Sita. Send this to the kindest person you know.

music_suggestions: A gentle, slowed flute or veena track from Instagram's library
caption:
POV: you finally get to clap back… and you don't 🕊️

After the war, Hanuman asked Sita for permission to punish the guards who had threatened her in Lanka. Sita said no: they were only following Ravana's orders, and no one never does wrong.

“पापानां वा शुभानां वा वधार्हाणां प्लवङ्गम । कार्यं करुणमार्येण न कश्चिन्नापराध्यति ॥”
Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 116.44 (with 116.30–42)

Today's lesson comes from Sita. Mercy > revenge. Day 16 of learning from Rama.
